rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: Suspected defective medicinal products are reported, investigated and, where necessary, recalled through the MHRA Defective Medicines Report Centre.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: The defective-medicines framework covers medicines and substances used in their manufacture or packaging.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: The framework does not cover adverse drug reactions, medical-device incidents or veterinary-medicine defects.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: MHRA introduced an online reporting form for industry stakeholders in the updated 2026 guide.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: MHRA advises people not to buy medicines through social media, messaging applications or unknown websites.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: Pharmacy-only and prescription medicines should be obtained from a UK-registered pharmacy.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: Members of the public can report suspected falsified medicines or suspicious sellers to MHRA.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: Yellow Card reports can include defective, fake or counterfeit medicines and medical devices.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: Medicine-defect risk depends on product identity, batch, supply chain, storage, packaging, source legitimacy, exposure and clinical use.

rows.source: MHRA defective and falsified-medicine controls
rows.verified: Defective or falsified-medicine evidence is product-, batch-, supplier-, patient- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level harm probability.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: The minimum legal tread depth for a car tyre is 1.6 millimetres.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Tyre pressures should be suitable for the vehicle load.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Drivers should inspect the full tyre, including the sidewall, for cuts and wear.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Under-inflated or over-inflated tyres can adversely affect braking, steering, fuel efficiency and tyre life.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Driving with illegal tyres can lead to a fine and penalty points for each tyre.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Recommended pressure may be shown inside the driver door, at the fuel cap or in the vehicle manual.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Checks before long journeys should include pressure, tread depth, tyre age and the spare tyre.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: DVSA market surveillance found part-worn tyres with penetrating objects, deep cuts or insufficient sale tread depth.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Road-tyre risk depends on pressure, tread, age, damage, load, speed, weather, maintenance and driving conditions.

rows.source: National Highways and DVSA road-tyre safety
rows.verified: Road-tyre evidence is vehicle-, tyre-, journey-, load-, weather- and driver-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
